verses.1: The apostles and the brothers who lived in Judea heard that the nations had accepted God’s message.
verses.2: When Peter went up to Jerusalem, the circumcised believers argued with him.
verses.3: They said, “You entered the house of uncircumcised men and ate with them.”
verses.4: Peter, beginning to explain to them one by one, said:
verses.5: “I was in the city of Joppa praying, and I saw a vision: something like a large sheet being let down from heaven, held by four corners, and it came all the way to me.
verses.6: Looking into it, I saw the four-footed animals of the earth, wild beasts, reptiles, and birds of the sky.
verses.7: I heard a voice saying to me, ‘Rise, Peter, kill and eat.’
verses.8: But I said, ‘Certainly not, Lord, for nothing common or unclean has ever entered my mouth.’
verses.9: A voice from heaven answered a second time, ‘What God has cleansed, you must not call common.’
verses.10: This happened three times, and immediately everything was taken up again into the heavens.
verses.11: Now just at that time three men stood at my house in the city where we were, having come from Caesarea to me.
verses.12: The Spirit told me without hesitation to go with them. And these six brothers came with me, and we entered the man’s house.
verses.13: He told us how he had seen an angel standing in his house and had said to him, ‘Send to Joppa and summon Simon who is called Peter,
verses.14: for he will speak words to you by which you and your entire household will be saved.’
verses.15: As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell upon them, just as he had fallen upon us at the beginning.
verses.16: I remembered the word of the Lord, how he said, ‘John indeed baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.’
verses.17: If then God gave the same gift to them as he gave to us who believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I to be able to hinder God?”
verses.18: When they heard this, they fell silent and glorified God, saying, “Then God has given repentance leading to life even to the Gentiles.”
verses.19: Now those who had been scattered because of the persecution that broke out when Stephen was killed traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, speaking the word to no one except to Jews.
verses.20: Among them, some Cypriots and Cyrenians came to Antioch and spoke to the Hellenists also, preaching the Lord Jesus.
verses.21: And the hand of the Lord was with them, and a large number who believed turned to the Lord.
verses.22: The report of these things reached the ears of the church in Jerusalem, and they sent Barnabas to Antioch.
verses.23: When he arrived and saw the grace of God, he was glad and encouraged everyone with wholehearted devotion to remain faithful to the Lord,
verses.24: for he was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and of faith, and a large crowd was added to the Lord.
verses.25: Then Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for Saul,
verses.26: and having found him, he brought him to Antioch. For a whole year they met together with the church and taught a great crowd. And in Antioch the disciples were first called Christians.
verses.27: Now in these days prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.
verses.28: One of them, named Agabus, stood up and predicted by the Spirit that there would be a great famine over the entire inhabited world, and it occurred during the reign of Claudius.
verses.29: The disciples, each as he was able and as prosperity allowed, decided that each of them would send aid to the brothers living in Judea,
verses.30: and that is what they did, sending it by the hands of Barnabas and Saul to the elders.

notes:
Notes
- v. 3: The term "circumcised" (ἐκ περιτομῆς) refers to Jewish believers who required others to follow Jewish customs.
- v. 18: “Repentance leading to life” (μετάνοιαν εἰς ζωὴν) is a direct translation of the phrase used in the Greek.
- v. 26: “Disciples were first called Christians” is a direct translation; "Christian" (Χριστιανούς) is a derived term from "Christ" (Χριστός).
